text: You need new software for a quick project. Sign up for a free trial or just a month, promising to cancel later. It feels like an easy, temporary fix.
Time flies, the project ends, and you completely forget. Then, a month later, your bank statement shows a charge. Another one. What just happened?
You frantically search for the cancellation button, diving through menus. It’s never obvious, always buried deep in obscure corners. They make it hard to leave.
This isn't accidental. The system sets "auto-renew" as the default. It's a "set it and forget it" mechanism, but you're not the one forgetting.
This subtle friction costs you. You pay for months you didn't need, simply because opting out took more effort than passive acceptance.
Now you see it. Every new subscription comes with a hidden default. Next time, you'll scrutinize those terms, knowing "auto-renew" is always waiting.
